gp.text: Continued pricing discipline and operational execution drove gross profit growth despite energy headwinds and challenging weather-related operating conditions throughout the quarter. Segment gross profit increased to $567 million ($9.47 per ton), and cash gross profit improved to $720 million ($12.02 per ton).

We use this metric to assess the operating performance of our business and as a basis for strategic planning and forecasting as we believe that it closely correlates to long-term shareholder value. We do not use this metric as a measure to allocate resources. We adjust EBITDA for certain items to provide a more consistent comparison of earnings performance from period to period. Concrete.heading: Asphalt and Concrete
Concrete.text: Non-aggregates segment gross profit in the second quarter was $58 million, and cash gross profit was $73 million. Asphalt gross profit margin remained strong at 15 percent, despite lower shipments due to weather and higher liquid asphalt costs. The prior year results included the Company’s Houston asphalt and construction business that was divested in the fourth quarter of 2025. Second quarter concrete results included two months of the Company’s California ready-mixed concrete business. The divestiture of these operations was completed in early June of 2026.

lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our top ten revenue producing states accounted for 90% of our 2025 revenues while our top five accounted for 63%.
Approximately 80% of our total aggregates shipments are delivered exclusively from the producing location to the customer by truck.
Approximately 15% of our total aggregates shipments are delivered by truck to the customer after reaching a sales yard by rail or water.
Less than 5% of aggregates shipments are delivered directly to the customer by rail or water.
In 2025, our five largest customers accounted for approximately 7% of our total revenues, and no single customer accounted for more than 2% of our total revenues.
The level of state and local spending on infrastructure varies across the United States and depends on individual state needs and economies.
This segment relies on our reserves of aggregates, functioning essentially as a customer to our aggregates operations.
No material part of our business depends upon any single customer whose loss would have a significant adverse effect on our business.

Our long-term success depends upon securing and permitting aggregates reserves in strategically located areas — Construction aggregates have a high weight-to-price ratio, and transportation costs can quickly exceed the cost of the aggregates.

Additionally, the calculation of mineral resources and reserves are estimates and depend upon geological interpretation and statistical inferences or assumptions drawn from drilling and sampling analysis.

Our future success depends upon attracting and retaining qualified personnel, particularly in sales and operations — Our success in attracting qualified personnel, particularly in the areas of sales and operations, is affected by changing demographics of the available pool of workers with the training and skills necessary to fill the available positions, the impact on the labor supply due to general economic conditions, and our ability to offer competitive compensation and benefit packages.
Our primary sources of liquidity are cash provided by our operating activities, a substantial, committed bank line of credit and our commercial paper program.
Realization of the deferred tax assets ultimately depends on the existence of sufficient taxable income of the appropriate character in either the carryback or carryforward period.

The accounting for gains and losses that result from changes in the fair value of derivative instruments depends on whether the derivatives have been designated and qualify as hedging instruments and the type of hedging relationship.

The ADP relies upon the RWQCB-approved expansion of the onsite Hewitt remedy and, necessarily, the two well head treatment systems operated by LADWP as the preferred method to address the off-site impacts that were the target of the 2017 AOC.
LADWP has alleged that the Hewitt Landfill is one of the primary sources of contamination at the NHW system and one of the sources of contamination at the NHC system.
